Tess (AE): Quick one — client hits 413 when POSTing a base64 archive to /v1/embeddings. Raw zip ~8.5MB -> base64 ~11.3MB. They get empty 413. Any short unblock?

Raj (SalesEng): Ask for their curl -v. Likely edge max_body_size or corporate proxy. Which flow do they prefer: single call or presigned upload?

Tess (AE): They expected single call for demo simplicity.

Kim (Support): Short fixes: 1) presigned PUT to S3 and send us pointer (recommended), 2) gzip binary and send application/octet-stream instead of base64-in-json, 3) split into smaller chunks and embed separately then aggregate.

edge-bot: nginx: client sent too large body (413), client=192.168.10.8, request="POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1"

Alex (Infra): We default to 10M at edge. We can grant a tenant-scoped temporary bump to 25M with Ops sign-off, TTL 48h. If their corporate proxy aborts earlier, presign path is the only reliable option.

Anya (Security): Presign with SSE-KMS + least-priv IAM role addresses compliance. We can include a short security note they can pass to security.

Raj (SalesEng): I'll prepare a tiny node script to: request presign -> PUT gzipped binary -> POST embeddings with input_url. Tess, want me to send now?

Tess (AE): Yes please. I'll ask them to run curl -v and share headers if 413 persists. End.
